2609.35070.title: Echoes of Deeds: Moral History Can Shape and Steer LLM Behavioral Choices
2609.35070.paper_summary: Evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) morality typically consider decisions in isolation, thus overlooking whether an individual's unrelated prior conduct influences the model's subsequent choices. This leaves open the question of whether, and to what extent, moral history shapes LLM decisional behaviors. Prior work on human moral decision-making shows that past behavior can influence subsequent moral choices. Building on this observation, we investigate whether analogous effects emerge in LLMs in two complementary ways: at the behavioral level, through the model's observable responses, and at the representation level, through its latent internal representations. We introduce MoralLedger, a framework for studying how an actor's moral history shapes actions for LLMs' behaviors under a fixed decision context. At the behavioral level, we find that prior moral histories systematically alter subsequent choices as a function of their valence and intensity. At the internal representation level, these histories induce a linearly recoverable direction in the residual stream that generalizes to held-out examples. Intervening along this direction on neutral-history prompts produces two-sided intensity-dependent changes in subsequent choices, with effects that are stronger than those induced by prompting alone or by favorable-nonmoral direction. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a latent representation of an actor's prior moral conduct can provide signed inference-time control over a moral decision. Our MoralLedger extends moral evaluation beyond static dilemmas, establishing moral history as both a source of behavioral sensitivity and a causal target for auditing and controlling moral behavior in LLMs.
2609.35070.paper_summary_zh: 評估大型語言模型（LLMs）的道德通常會孤立地考慮決策，因此忽略了個體無關的先前行為是否會影響模型後續的選擇。這使得一個問題懸而未決：道德歷史在多大程度上塑造了LLM的決策行為。先前關於人類道德決策的研究顯示，過去的行為可以影響後續的道德選擇。在這一觀察的基礎上，我們探討了類似的效應是否在LLMs中以兩種互補的方式出現：在行為層面，通過模型的可觀察反應；在表示層面，通過其潛在的內部表示。我們引入了MoralLedger，一個研究演員的道德歷史如何在固定決策背景下塑造LLMs行為的框架。在行為層面，我們發現先前的道德歷史系統性地改變後續選擇，這取決於其價值和強度。在內部表示層面，這些歷史在殘差流中引發了一個線性可恢復的方向，並且對保留的示例具有普遍性。在中立歷史提示上沿著這一方向進行干預會產生雙向強度依賴的後續選擇變化，其效果比單獨提示或有利的非道德方向所引發的效果更強。據我們所知，這是首次展示演員先前道德行為的潛在表示可以在道德決策上提供簽名推斷時間控制。我們的MoralLedger將道德評估擴展到靜態困境之外，確立道德歷史作為行為敏感性的來源和審計及控制LLMs道德行為的因果目標。
